hypothesis: Consecutive matching current-scan object shapes can provide temporal evidence of a currently measured corridor intrusion without accumulating points through a rejected odometric transform.
design: Use the existing association only to propose correspondence; require reciprocal nearest-support overlap of centered sensor-frame shapes on consecutive acquisitions.
The radius is two existing 5 cm support voxels, fixed before replay; overlap is symmetric so a tiny subset of infrastructure cannot explain a large shape.

Each contributing scan must independently have a measured intersecting relation, existing minimum support and at least the existing claim_min_support_voxels of certified unexplained interior evidence.
Do not use odometry rotation/translation, pooled world support, synthetic intensity/source labels, bag names or frame numbers for this channel.
Only add a separately named confirmation route when current odometry is rejected. Keep positional uncertainty and all calibration caveats; never rewrite motion validity.
Pose-based counters retain their original meaning; local temporal recurrence is not independent physical firing evidence or calibrated probability.

acceptance.synthetic: Both organizer events9 and10 obtain exact-provenance confirmed intersection on at least two consecutive acquisitions; previously confirmed positive events are retained. Outside-contour disagreement5/7 is reported unchanged, not scored away.
acceptance.real_negatives: On the fixed2641-frame initial regression panel, confirmed-intersection episode count and alarm-frame count do not increase on any organizer-declared negative recording, and unknown coverage does not grow to hide alarms.
acceptance.person: The36 author-reviewed person frames retain observed support and presence without new confirmed intersection; no increase in non-target alarm frames in that interval.
acceptance.promotion: A failed criterion rejects default promotion; preserve failed outputs and report the tradeoff. Passing this initial gate is not a claim of completed full20-minute evaluation or closure of issues21/23.
